$comment: Catalog of release trains. A train is a set of packages that release together because they depend on each other in a line. Adding a package, or a whole new train, is an edit here followed by `node .github/scripts/sync-release-trains.mjs`; nothing else hardcodes the list. See .github/scripts/lib/release-trains.mjs.

sdk.description: The SDK chain: the engine, the SDK on top of it, and the agent stack that consumes the CLI.

engine.description: @qvac/inference and @qvac/sdk share a major and minor; packages/sdk lint enforces it.

postPublish.$comment: Tag only. The Releases page is the SDK's; the engine's notes ride in the SDK release for the version it depends on.

agentstack.description: Consumers of the CLI. Each moves on its own version.

sidecars.name: tetherto-qvac-sdk
sidecars.description: Generated from @qvac/sdk and published at the same version. Not an npm package, so nx release does not carry it.

assets.$comment: Release assets a project can declare in postPublish.assets. Each maps to a job in release-train.yml — `uses:` must be a literal, so adding one is a catalog entry plus a job, not a catalog entry alone.

sdk-python-fat-wheels.description: Self-contained per-platform tetherto-qvac-sdk wheels, attached to the release so `pip install -f <release>` needs no separate worker.

nx.$comment: Written into nx.json's `release` block by sync-release-trains.mjs. Each value is set because the nx default does the wrong thing here. There is deliberately no releaseTag pattern: nx tags a fixed group once, with no {projectName} to interpolate, while this repo tags each package as <slug>-v<version> after its publish succeeds. Tagging stays in release-train.yml.
